And in settling the problem, in addition to local institutions, institutions at republican level joined in which further complicated the situation and reached a critical point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Among the facts that you have mentioned, the material facts, that is that the strike went on for months and that one of the demands was the replacement of the manager, as far as I know anything about strikes, there's hardly a single workers' strike, particularly those that last for some time, that don't include the demand for a replacement of the manager. Explain to me, please, what is the alleged political motivation for the strike. Do you have any other arguments apart from this one, that they wanted the director replaced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: Also their refusal to go back to work and join the regular work process. They persisted on separation and subsequently the formation of a parallel company with the resources they had received from Serbia. I mean vehicles, material resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the workers of a transport company? You say that later on, certain individuals -- some of the strikers could later be seen within the ranks of the Serbian Democratic Party. That's what you said a moment ago. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Party of Democratic Action, that is the Muslim party, was founded far before the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date as to when which one was formed, but I don't exclude that what you are saying is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the 27th of March, 1990, the initiating committee of the Party of Democratic Action declared that the party would be formed in May. On behalf of that board, Alija Izetbegovic, at a press conference in Sarajevo, said that, "The SDA --" and he is being quoted -- "is a political association of citizens of Yugoslavia belonging to the Muslim cultural historical circle but also of other citizens." Those who belong to the Muslim cultural historical circle, as he put it. Are you familiar with that? This was on the 27th of March, 1990.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: At that time, the SDA did not in any way get implicated into the dispute with the workers of Focatrans.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And when did that dispute start?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: In the first half of 1990 when workers of Serb ethnicity separated and started their strike.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that it was only the Serbs that were on strike in Focatrans?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: Workers of Serb ethnicity mostly. There may have been a couple of Serbs who stayed on working, but I'm talking about the vast majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And were the Serbs in the vast majority among the employees of Focatrans?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: I don't know the exact percentage share, but I don't think that there was a drastic difference in terms of the number of employed Serbs or Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And were there Muslims who were also striking, on strike?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: I don't have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you claiming that not a single Muslim took part in the strike?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: No, I'm not claiming that, but I don't have the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And what was the population composition in Foca before the war, according to the 1991 census? What was the ratio between Muslims and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: The largest community were the Bosniaks, or Muslims, then followed by the Serbs, and there was about 18 or 19 per cent of those who declared themselves to be Yugoslavs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So one-fifth were Yugoslavs in Foca.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: I think about 18 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what was the percentage share of the Serbs, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: I think about 38 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Together with the Yugoslavs, that makes it 56 per cent. Are you telling us that 44 per cent of the population in Foca were Muslims? You surely know the figures from the 1991 census.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: I don't know the exact figures just now, but I do know that the Muslim population was the largest, followed by the Serbs, and that there was a certain percentage of people who declared themselves Yugoslavs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In that case, I won't persist, as there are figures about all that. In your statement you say that you are not a member of the SDA but the SDA appointed you to the position that you held.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were proposed by the SDA. So there is every reason to believe that you must have known what was -- what the SDA was doing in Foca, your closeness with it, because otherwise they wouldn't have proposed you to such an important post. You must have been close to them and they wouldn't have proposed you if they didn't trust you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: If I were to give you a more detailed answer to this question, then in my answer I would have to reveal my identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I won't insist, then, but another reason for being familiar with the situation and activity of that party in that town is your formal

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will go into private session for the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to comment, Mr. 1531, since we have already mentioned Halid Cengic, could you please comment part of an interview granted to the Sarajevo weekly Liljan issue 279, pages 11 to 13, under a heading Interview of the Week, Cengic, the main logistics person of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, a soldier and a Hadzija. In this interview, Cengic mentions information about the activities of the SDA in Foca which I would say you must have been familiar with. According to what Halid Cengic says, "The Muslims in Foca, as early as the 1st of August, 1990, allegedly to defend Focatrans, had a platoon of men armed with automatic weapons, a machine-gun, and a mortar. They all had camouflage uniforms, and they took their oaths at the Ustikolina mosque with their hands on the Koran." This is a quotation from this interview. I would say this is something that you should, and I would even say you must have known for the reasons I have given. Are you aware of this, Mr. 1531?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1531
utterances.text: In view of your question, it would have been better if we hadn't gone back into open session for me to be able to explain some things to Their Honours, the Prosecution, and you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now until tomorrow morning, 9.00. Mr. Milosevic, you have 20 minutes left with this witness. Mr. B-1531, could I please remind you, as we remind all witnesses, not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over. Very well. We will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of November, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
